chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated from al-Ash'ari, from Samakah ibn Mihran, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Verily, when Allah, the Exalted, created Adam (peace be upon him), He blew into him from His spirit. The first thing that was blown into him from His spirit was his intellect ('Aql). Then He blew into him, and the first thing Allah created from the intellect of Adam (peace be upon him) was the Will/Testament (Al-Wasiyyah).'

He (Abu Abdillah) said: 'And this is what Allah wrote upon the children of Adam (peace be upon him). It is that which Allah commanded in the Book (Quran). It is that which Ibrahim bequeathed to Ishaq and Ya'qub. It is that which Ya'qub bequeathed to his sons. It is that which Yusuf bequeathed to his brothers. It is that which Musa bequeathed to Harun and his brother. It is that which Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) bequeathed to his family and companions. And it is that which the Imams (peace be upon them) bequeathed to their Shia and their families.'
ai.seo_question: What is the divine origin and significance of Al-Wasiyyah (the Will) in Shia theology?
ai.summary: In *Kamal al-Din*, Shaykh al-Saduq uses this hadith to ground the Shia doctrine of *Nass* (divine designation) in primordial cosmology, presenting the *Wasi* (successor) as the first intellectual emanation from Adam. This establishes the Imamate not merely as a political appointment but as an eternal, metaphysical reality that predates creation and persists through all prophetic dispensations. It underscores the continuity of divine guidance, linking the authority of the Prophet directly to the Imams as the custodians of the *Wasiyyah*.
